claim: Mouse YTHDC2 is a mammalian homolog of Drosophila Bgcn, identified by tBlastn analysis with an E-value of 9e−78.
source: Analysis by tBlastn of the nr/nt mouse and human databases using the Drosophila Bgcn protein sequence identified mouse YTHDC2 (E-value = 9e−78) and human YTHDC2 (E-value = 2e−61) as mammalian homologs (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from tBlastn analysis showing sequence similarity between Drosophila Bgcn and mouse YTHDC2.

claim: Human YTHDC2 is a mammalian homolog of Drosophila Bgcn, identified by tBlastn analysis with an E-value of 2e−61.
source: Analysis by tBlastn of the nr/nt mouse and human databases using the Drosophila Bgcn protein sequence identified mouse YTHDC2 (E-value = 9e−78) and human YTHDC2 (E-value = 2e−61) as mammalian homologs (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from tBlastn analysis showing sequence similarity between Drosophila Bgcn and human YTHDC2.

claim: Mouse YTHDC2 shares approximately 44–55% sequence similarity with Drosophila Bgcn within each conserved domain.
source: Mouse YTHDC2, like Drosophila Bgcn, is a member of the DEAD/DExH box family of RNA helicases and shares with Drosophila Bgcn the signature DExH RNA helicase domain, a helicase-associated domain (HA2), and several other protein domains, having approximately 44–55% sequence similarity to Drosophila Bgcn within each domain (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence comparison data shown in Figure 1B and described in the text.

claim: The YTH domain present in mouse and other vertebrate YTHDC2 homologs was not recognized in Drosophila Bgcn.
source: The YTH domain, present in the mouse and other vertebrate homologs, was not recognized in Drosophila Bgcn.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis comparing mouse YTHDC2 and Drosophila Bgcn protein domains.

claim: Mouse YTHDC2 protein is expressed in adult testis but not in several other adult tissues examined.
source: Western blot analysis of adult mouse tissues detected YTHDC2 protein in testis but not in several other adult tissues examined (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: YTHDC2 is strongly expressed in spermatocytes that co-express the meiotic marker SYCP3.
source: YTHDC2 was not detected by immunofluorescence in spermatogonia next to the tubule wall but was strongly expressed in spermatocytes that co-expressed the meiotic marker SYCP3 (Figure 1D–F), suggesting that mouse YTHDC2 is up-regulated in germ cells upon entry into meiosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 1D-F.

claim: Mouse YTHDC2 is up-regulated in germ cells upon entry into meiosis.
source: YTHDC2 was not detected by immunofluorescence in spermatogonia next to the tubule wall but was strongly expressed in spermatocytes that co-expressed the meiotic marker SYCP3 (Figure 1D–F), suggesting that mouse YTHDC2 is up-regulated in germ cells upon entry into meiosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from immunofluorescence data showing YTHDC2 expression pattern in different germ cell stages.

claim: YTHDC2 localizes primarily to the cytoplasm in mouse spermatocytes.
source: Immunofluorescence staining of cross-sections of adult mouse testis tubules revealed YTHDC2 in a subset of germ cells in a majority of the seminiferous tubules (Figure 1D), where the protein localized primarily to the cytoplasm (Figure 1E), similar to Drosophila Bgcn.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Human YTHDC2 is not detected in germ cells around the periphery of the testis tubule but is present in the cytoplasm of DDX4-positive germ cells positioned further inward.
source: Staining cross-sections of human testis tubules with anti-YTHDC2 revealed an expression pattern similar to that observed in mouse, with human YTHDC2 not detected in germ cells around the periphery of the testis tubule (Figure 1G–I, arrowheads), but present in the cytoplasm of a subset of DDX4-positive germ cells positioned further inward, including pachytene spermatocytes marked by staining of the sex vesicle by γ-H2AX (Figure 1J, arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data from human testis sections shown in Figures 1G-J.

claim: Expression of mouse YTHDC2 protein increased between postnatal day 10 to day 12 (P10-P12), the stage when the first wave of early germ cells initiate meiotic prophase.
source: Consistent with the expression pattern of both mouse and human YTHDC2 in the adult testis, analysis of mouse YTHDC2 protein levels during the first wave of spermatogenesis in testes from juvenile males by both western blot (Figure 1K) and immunofluorescence staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C′) revealed that expression of YTHDC2 increased between postnatal day 10 to day 12 (P10-P12), the stage when the first wave of early germ cells initiate meiotic prophase.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1K and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C′.

claim: Ythdc2 RNA levels started to increase at P10 and peaked at P14 during the first wave of spermatogenesis.
source: Likewise, analysis of published RNA-Seq data from the first wave of spermatogenesis (Margolin et al., 2014) showed that Ythdc2 RNA levels started to increase at P10 and peaked at P14, when pachytene spermatocytes are present (Figure 1L and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data from a published study (Margolin et al., 2014) shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Mice homozygous mutant for either the Ythdc2 targeted trap allele or the null allele were viable and born at the expected Mendelian ratio.
source: Similar to bgcn-/- flies, mice homozygous mutant for either the Ythdc2 targeted trap allele or the null allele were viable, born at the expected Mendelian ratio (Supplementary file 1) and developed normally, except that Ythdc2-/- female mice gained weight more rapidly than wild-type controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data showing Mendelian ratios in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Ythdc2-/- female mice gained weight more rapidly than wild-type controls.
source: Similar to bgcn-/- flies, mice homozygous mutant for either the Ythdc2 targeted trap allele or the null allele were viable, born at the expected Mendelian ratio (Supplementary file 1) and developed normally, except that Ythdc2-/- female mice gained weight more rapidly than wild-type controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by weight measurement data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Adult male Ythdc2 homozygous mutant mice were infertile.
source: Adult male Ythdc2 homozygous mutant mice were infertile (Supplementary file 2), had small testes that weighed significantly less compared to wild-type littermate controls (Figure 2A–C) and completely lacked mature spermatozoa in the epididymis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by fertility testing data shown in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Ythdc2-/- male mice had small testes that weighed significantly less compared to wild-type littermate controls.
source: Adult male Ythdc2 homozygous mutant mice were infertile (Supplementary file 2), had small testes that weighed significantly less compared to wild-type littermate controls (Figure 2A–C) and completely lacked mature spermatozoa in the epididymis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by testis weight measurements shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: Ythdc2-/- male mice completely lacked mature spermatozoa in the epididymis.
source: Adult male Ythdc2 homozygous mutant mice were infertile (Supplementary file 2), had small testes that weighed significantly less compared to wild-type littermate controls (Figure 2A–C) and completely lacked mature spermatozoa in the epididymis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis of epididymis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Cross-sections of testis seminiferous tubules from 8-week-old Ythdc2-/- males revealed major degeneration of germ cells compared to wild-type controls.
source: Cross-sections of testis seminiferous tubules from 8-week-old males revealed major degeneration of germ cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules compared to wild-type controls (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Ythdc2-/- tubules contained spermatogonia as well as preleptotene spermatocytes with nuclear morphology similar to wild type at P30.
source: Examination of histological sections from P30 testes at high magnification revealed that Ythdc2-/- tubules contained spermatogonia as well as preleptotene spermatocytes with nuclear morphology similar to wild type (Figure 2F,F' and and G,G′′, black arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2F,F' and G,G′′.

claim: Normal appearing preleptotene cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules frequently had cells nearby that either had highly condensed chromosomes or appeared apoptotic.
source: However, normal appearing preleptotene cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules frequently had cells nearby that either had highly condensed chromosomes (Figure 2G,G′, red arrowhead and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E) or appeared apoptotic (Figure 2G,G′′′, red arrow and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2G,G′, G′′′ and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Both metaphase and anaphase figures were detected near preleptotene spermatocytes in Ythdc2-/- tubules.
source: Both metaphase and anaphase figures were detected near preleptotene spermatocytes in Ythdc2-/- tubules (Figure 2H–H′'and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), suggesting that the abnormal metaphase cells had attempted to divide.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2H–H′' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The abnormal metaphase cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules had attempted to divide.
source: Both metaphase and anaphase figures were detected near preleptotene spermatocytes in Ythdc2-/- tubules (Figure 2H–H′'and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), suggesting that the abnormal metaphase cells had attempted to divide.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of both metaphase and anaphase figures in the mutant.

claim: Some P30 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained germ cells entering the leptotene stage of meiotic prophase, though not as frequently as in age-matched wild-type tubules.
source: Although not as frequently as in age-matched wild-type tubules, some P30 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained germ cells entering the leptotene stage of meiotic prophase (Figure 2I,I′, black arrow and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2I,I′ and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Ythdc2-/- tubules lacked late spermatocyte and spermatid stages seen in wild-type tubules at P30.
source: However, Ythdc2-/- tubules lacked late spermatocyte and spermatid stages seen in wild-type tubules (Figure 2F,F′′, outlined arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2F,F′′.

claim: The transition from the preleptotene or leptotene stage, to abnormal chromosome condensation, to cell death appeared to occur rapidly in Ythdc2-/- testes.
source: The transition from the preleptotene or leptotene stage, to abnormal chromosome condensation, to cell death appeared to occur rapidly, as all three stages were often observed within the same seminiferous tubule section in Ythdc2-/- testes (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of multiple stages within the same tubule section.

claim: TUNEL staining of P30 testes showed an increased number of TUNEL-positive cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules compared to wild type.
source: TUNEL staining of P30 testes showed an increased number of TUNEL-positive cells in Ythdc2-/- tubules compared to wild type (Figure 2J–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 2J–L.

claim: At P8, Ythdc2-/- testis tubules were filled with spermatogonia that appeared normal compared to wild-type littermate controls.
source: At P8, the time point when most germ cells are at the spermatogonial stage, Ythdc2-/- testis tubules were filled with spermatogonia that appeared normal compared to wild-type littermate controls (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Germ cells in Ythdc2-/- testes began to show abnormalities at P10, when the first wave of germ cells normally initiate meiotic prophase.
source: However, germ cells in Ythdc2-/- testes began to show abnormalities at P10, when the first wave of germ cells normally initiate meiotic prophase.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis during the first wave of spermatogenesis.

claim: Although Ythdc2-/- tubules at P10 contained histologically normal preleptotene spermatocytes, many tubules had germ cells that started to condense their chromosomes.
source: In contrast, although Ythdc2-/- tubules at P10 contained histologically normal preleptotene spermatocytes (Figure 3D, black arrows and inset), many tubules from P10 Ythdc2-/- mice had germ cells that started to condense their chromosomes, as if trying to divide rather than entering the normally extended meiotic prophase period (Figure 3D, red arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Some P12 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained leptotene spermatocytes and a few contained zygotene spermatocytes.
source: While some P12 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained leptotene spermatocytes (Figure 3F, black arrowheads and inset) and a few contained zygotene spermatocytes (Figure 3I), many tubules contained germ cells with condensed chromosomes (Figure 3J, red arrowheads and inset, and 3K) rarely seen in age-matched wild-type testes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3F and 3I.

claim: Many P12 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained germ cells with condensed chromosomes rarely seen in age-matched wild-type testes.
source: While some P12 Ythdc2-/- tubules contained leptotene spermatocytes (Figure 3F, black arrowheads and inset) and a few contained zygotene spermatocytes (Figure 3I), many tubules contained germ cells with condensed chromosomes (Figure 3J, red arrowheads and inset, and 3K) rarely seen in age-matched wild-type testes.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3J and 3K.

claim: No pachytene spermatocytes were observed in P14 Ythdc2-/- testis tubules.
source: By P14, many germ cells had entered the pachytene stage of meiotic prophase in wild-type testes (Figure 3G, outlined arrowheads and inset, and 3L-L′′). However, no pachytene spermatocytes were observed in P14 Ythdc2-/- testis tubules and many tubules still contained germ cells with condensed chromosomes (Figure 3H, red arrowheads and inset).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: 95% of Ythdc2-/- germ cells with condensed chromosomes at P14 had 40 chromosomes, similar to a mitotic division, rather than 20 paired bivalents typical for meiosis I.
source: Analysis of P14 chromosome spreads, in which abnormal Ythdc2-/- germ cells with condensed chromosomes were distinguished from mitotic nuclei based on their expression of the meiotic marker SYCP3, revealed that 95% of Ythdc2-/- germ cells with condensed chromosomes had 40 chromosomes (Figure 3M–M′'and 3N), similar to a mitotic division, rather than 20 paired bivalents typical for meiosis I.
evidence: The claim is supported by chromosome spread analysis shown in Figure 3M–M′' and 3N.

claim: SYCP3 appeared to localize to foci at the ends of the condensed chromosomes in Ythdc2-/- germ cells rather than along the chromosomes as in wild type.
source: In addition, SYCP3 appeared to localize to foci at the ends of the condensed chromosomes in Ythdc2-/- germ cells (Figure 3M–M′′) rather than along the chromosomes as in wild type (Figure 3L–L′′).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis of chromosome spreads shown in Figure 3L–L′′ and 3M–M′′.

claim: The expression pattern of STRA8 protein in Ythdc2-/- testes was similar to wild type.
source: The expression pattern of STRA8 protein in Ythdc2-/- testes was similar to wild type (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: After a short pulse of EdU followed by a 2 hr chase, many germ cells were positive for both STRA8 and EdU in Ythdc2-/- testes, indicating that preleptotene spermatocytes were successfully undergoing premeiotic DNA synthesis.
source: After a short pulse of EdU followed by a 2 hr chase, many germ cells were positive for both STRA8 and EdU, indicating that preleptotene spermatocytes in Ythdc2-/- testes were successfully undergoing premeiotic DNA synthesis, similar to wild type (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Both wild-type and YTHDC2-deficient germ cells stained positive for the meiotic cohesion REC8.
source: Both wild-type and YTHDC2-deficient germ cells stained positive for the meiotic cohesion REC8 (Figure 4E), an early meiotic marker expressed starting in the preleptotene stage.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Both wild-type and Ythdc2-/- P14 spreads showed nuclei with SYCP3 expression, confirming that some Ythdc2 mutant germ cells enter the early stages of meiotic prophase.
source: Both wild-type and Ythdc2-/- P14 spreads also showed nuclei with SYCP3 expression (Figure 4F), confirming that some Ythdc2 mutant germ cells enter the early stages of meiotic prophase.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis of germ cell spreads shown in Figure 4F.

claim: YTHDC2-deficient germ cells can reach leptotene and early zygotene spermatocyte stages.
source: Analysis of germ cell spreads confirmed that YTHDC2-deficient germ cells can reach leptotene (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and early zygotene (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) spermatocyte stages.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis of germ cell spreads shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: High levels of DMC1 were detected by immunofluorescence in only a small percentage of Ythdc2-/- tubules at P12, in contrast to the high levels in wild-type spermatocytes.
source: In contrast to the high levels of DMC1 protein in wild-type spermatocytes at P12, high levels of DMC1 were detected by immunofluorescence in only a small percentage of Ythdc2-/- tubules (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Analysis of expression of Spo11 mRNA in testis extracts showed a decrease in Ythdc2 mutant compared to wild-type testes at P14.
source: Analysis of expression of Spo11 mRNA in testis extracts showed a decrease in Ythdc2 mutant compared to wild-type testes at P14 (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: By P14, most tubule cross-sections from wild type had high levels of SYCP3 that localized along the entire length of the chromosomes.
source: By P14, most tubule cross-sections from wild type had high levels of SYCP3 that localized along the entire length of the chromosomes (Figure 4K,L).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4K,L.

claim: While SYCP3 was observed in some Ythdc2-/- testes tubule cross-sections at P14, the level of SYCP3 protein detected was usually low and often localized in a punctate pattern.
source: In contrast, while SYCP3 was observed in some Ythdc2-/- testes tubule cross-sections at P14 (Figure 4M), the level of SYCP3 protein detected was usually low and often localized in a punctate pattern, as in earlier stages of meiosis (Figure 4N).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4M,N.

claim: Ythdc2-/- adult female mice were infertile and had thin uteri and small ovaries compared to wild type.
source: Ythdc2-/- adult female mice were infertile and had thin uteri and small ovaries compared to wild type (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Ovaries from adult Ythdc2-/- mice completely lacked developing follicles.
source: Ovaries from adult Ythdc2-/- mice completely lacked developing follicles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: No germinal vesicles were detected in P21 Ythdc2-/- ovaries, while P21 wild-type ovaries contained full-grown oocytes in germinal vesicles.
source: While P21 wild-type ovaries contained full-grown oocytes in germinal vesicles (Figure 5C), no germinal vesicles were detected in P21 Ythdc2-/- ovaries (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: No primordial follicles were detected in P5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries, while wild-type ovaries at P5 were filled with primordial follicles.
source: At P5, when wild-type ovaries were filled with primordial follicles, no primordial follicles were detected in Ythdc2-/- ovaries (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: At birth (P0.5), Ythdc2-/- ovaries contained some DDX4+ germ cells, but many fewer than in aged-matched wild-type ovaries.
source: At birth (P0.5), Ythdc2-/- ovaries contained some DDX4+ germ cells, but many fewer than in aged-matched wild-type ovaries (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G), suggesting that YTHDC2 function is required during the fetal period for survival of female germ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G.

claim: YTHDC2 function is required during the fetal period for survival of female germ cells.
source: At birth (P0.5), Ythdc2-/- ovaries contained some DDX4+ germ cells, but many fewer than in aged-matched wild-type ovaries (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G), suggesting that YTHDC2 function is required during the fetal period for survival of female germ cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of reduced germ cell numbers in Ythdc2-/- ovaries at birth.

claim: At E14.5, Ythdc2-/- ovaries contained many premeiotic germ cells that appeared similar to those in wild type.
source: At E14.5, Ythdc2-/- ovaries contained many premeiotic germ cells that appeared similar to those in wild type (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: By E15.5, YTHDC2-deficient germ cells did not show the chromosomal changes characteristic of meiotic prophase, but instead showed nuclear morphology resembling premeiotic cells.
source: By E15.5, however, when many wild-type germ cells had entered meiotic prophase (Figure 5G), YTHDC2-deficient germ cells did not show the chromosomal changes characteristic of meiotic prophase, but instead showed nuclear morphology resembling premeiotic cells (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: At E16.5, Ythdc2-/- germ cells showed abnormal chromatin condensation, while wild-type germ cells were clearly progressing through meiotic prophase.
source: At E16.5, when wild-type germ cells were clearly progressing through meiotic prophase (Figure 5I), Ythdc2-/- germ cells showed abnormal chromatin condensation (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5I,J.

claim: YTHDC2 protein was up-regulated at E15.5 in wild type in germ cells that co-expressed the meiotic marker SYCP3.
source: Consistent with the appearance of defects in germ cells in E15.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries, YTHDC2 protein was up-regulated at E15.5 in wild type (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H) in germ cells that co-expressed the meiotic marker SYCP3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining of E14.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries revealed similar levels and distribution of STRA8 protein as in age-matched wild-type ovaries.
source: The apparent defects in the transition from mitosis to meiosis seen in Ythdc2-/- ovaries were not due to low levels of STRA8, as immunofluorescence staining of E14.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries revealed similar levels and distribution of STRA8 protein as in age-matched wild-type ovaries (Figure 5K,L).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5K,L.

claim: Some germ cells in Ythdc2-/- ovaries expressed SYCP3 at E15.5, suggesting that some YTHDC2-deficient female germ cells enter the early stages of meiosis.
source: Some germ cells in Ythdc2-/- ovaries expressed SYCP3 at E15.5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J,K), suggesting that, as in the male, some YTHDC2-deficient female germ cells enter the early stages of meiosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1J,K and inferred from the SYCP3 expression pattern.

claim: Few YTHDC2-deficient female germ cells expressed DMC1 at E15.5, in contrast to the abundant expression of DMC1 in age-matched wild-type ovaries.
source: Also similar to males, few YTHDC2-deficient female germ cells expressed DMC1 at E15.5 (Figure 5N), in contrast to the abundant expression of DMC1 in age-matched wild-type ovaries (Figure 5M).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5M,N.

claim: Expression of the G1 mitotic marker Cyclin D1 appeared to persist in many germ cells in Ythdc2-/- ovaries at E15.5, while very few germ cells expressed Cyclin D1 in wild-type ovaries at this stage.
source: Consistent with failure of Ythdc2-/- female germ cells to properly transition from mitotic divisions to meiotic prophase, expression of the G1 mitotic marker Cyclin D1 appeared to persist in many germ cells in Ythdc2-/- ovaries at E15.5 (Figure 5P), while very few germ cells expressed Cyclin D1 in wild-type ovaries at this stage (Figure 5O).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5O,P.

claim: 16% of DDX4+ germ cells stained positive for pH3 in E16.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries compared to only 1.4% in wild-type ovaries at E16.5.
source: However, consistent with the abnormal condensation of chromosomes observed in histological sections (Figure 5J), 16% of DDX4+ germ cells stained positive for pH3 in E16.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries (Figure 5R and Figure 5—figure supplement 1L) compared to only 1.4% in wild-type ovaries at E16.5 (Figure 5Q and Figure 5—figure supplement 1L), suggesting that in the absence of YTHDC2 function, female germ cells failed to properly implement meiotic prophase in the fetal ovary.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 5Q,R and Figure 5—figure supplement 1L.

claim: In the absence of YTHDC2 function, female germ cells failed to properly implement meiotic prophase in the fetal ovary.
source: However, consistent with the abnormal condensation of chromosomes observed in histological sections (Figure 5J), 16% of DDX4+ germ cells stained positive for pH3 in E16.5 Ythdc2-/- ovaries (Figure 5R and Figure 5—figure supplement 1L) compared to only 1.4% in wild-type ovaries at E16.5 (Figure 5Q and Figure 5—figure supplement 1L), suggesting that in the absence of YTHDC2 function, female germ cells failed to properly implement meiotic prophase in the fetal ovary.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased pH3 staining and abnormal chromosome condensation in Ythdc2-/- ovaries.

claim: The Ythdc2 mutant phenotype is similar to the Meioc mutant phenotype in both males and females.
source: The Ythdc2 mutant phenotype is similar to the Meioc mutant phenotype in both males and females (Abby et al., 2016; Soh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with published studies on Meioc mutants.

claim: Immunoprecipitation from testis extracts showed that YTHDC2 physically interacts with MEIOC.
source: Consistent with this, immunoprecipitation from testis extracts showed that YTHDC2 physically interacts with MEIOC (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that the two proteins may work together to promote progression through meiotic prophase.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: YTHDC2 and MEIOC may work together to promote progression through meiotic prophase.
source: Consistent with this, immunoprecipitation from testis extracts showed that YTHDC2 physically interacts with MEIOC (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that the two proteins may work together to promote progression through meiotic prophase.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the physical interaction between YTHDC2 and MEIOC and the similarity of their mutant phenotypes.

claim: Meioc RNA expression was not significantly different in P12 Ythdc2-/- testes compared to wild type.
source: Meioc RNA expression was not significantly different in P12 Ythdc2-/- testes compared to wild type (Figure 8C and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: MEIOC protein levels were much lower in Ythdc2-/- P12 testes than in wild type, being barely detected by western blot or by immunofluorescence staining.
source: However, MEIOC protein levels were much lower in Ythdc2-/- P12 testes than in wild type, being barely detected by western blot (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B) or by immunofluorescence staining (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D) in the mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B,D.

claim: Comparison of the mRNAs expressed in Ythdc2-/- and age-matched wild-type testes at P12 and P14 by RNA sequencing revealed a large number of transcripts that were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- testes than in age-matched wild-type testes.
source: Comparison of the mRNAs expressed in Ythdc2-/- and age-matched wild-type testes at P12 (Figure 6A) and P14 (Figure 6B) by RNA sequencing revealed a large number of transcripts (959 transcripts at P14, adjusted p-value<0.05) that were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- testes than in age-matched wild-type testes.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: 959 transcripts at P14 were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- testes than in age-matched wild-type testes (adjusted p-value<0.05).
source: Comparison of the mRNAs expressed in Ythdc2-/- and age-matched wild-type testes at P12 (Figure 6A) and P14 (Figure 6B) by RNA sequencing revealed a large number of transcripts (959 transcripts at P14, adjusted p-value<0.05) that were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- testes than in age-matched wild-type testes.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: 199 transcripts at P12 were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- than in wild-type testes.
source: While the changes at P12 were subtle, the trend was similar: 199 transcripts were expressed at lower levels in Ythdc2-/- than in wild-type testes.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: The transcripts most under-expressed in Ythdc2-/- compared to age-matched wild-type testes were frequently up-regulated in spermatocytes compared to spermatogonia based on data from sorted germ cells.
